blogs.title: Why Byte-Level Models Are the Future of AI: Meet the Byte Latent Transformer
blogs.description: An introductory post that explains why tokenization has been a bottleneck for large language models, how BLTs learn directly from raw bytes, and why this “byte‑first” approach offers flexibility, robustness, and better scaling in plain language.

blogs.title: Patch, Patch, Patch: The Clever Trick That Lets BLTs Do More with Less
blogs.description: A deep dive into BLT’s dynamic patching mechanism—how it splits sequences based on entropy, why variable‑sized patches allocate compute where it matters, and how this compares to static‑width strides and whitespace segmentation.

blogs.title: The Triple‑Headed Power of BLT: Local Encoders, Decoders, and a Global Latent Transformer
blogs.description: "Architectural tea‑time" – walk through the three key components of BLT, explain how the lightweight encoders/decoders feed into a heavyweight latent transformer, and show why this composition beats traditional token‑based transformers at scale.

blogs.title: From Corrupt Code to Clean Answers: How Byte Transformers Handle Noise Better
blogs.description: A case study on BLT’s robustness. Compare standard LLMs to byte‑centric models when faced with scrambled letters, missing characters, or mixed‑case attacks—illustrating real‑world scenarios where BLTs shine.

blogs.title: Scaling Up Without Paying the Price: How Bigger Patches Let BLTs Grow Efficiently
blogs.description: Explain the fixed‑inference‑flop scaling experiments that demonstrate BLT’s unique ability to increase model size while keeping inference costs constant by simply enlarging patch size—something tokenizers just can’t do.
